bibliographic.title: Sobre a eficiência da ética como ferramenta de governança da inteligência artificial
bibliographic.authors: Nicholas Kluge Corrêa; Nythamar Fernandes de Oliveira; Diogo Fernando Massmann
bibliographic.venue: Veritas (Porto Alegre) - Revista de Filosofia da PUCRS
bibliographic.citation_apa: Corrêa, N. K., Oliveira, N. F. de, & Massmann, D. F. (2022). Sobre a eficiência da ética como ferramenta de governança da inteligência artificial. Veritas (Porto Alegre), 67(1), 1-11. https://doi.org/10.15448/1984-6746.2022.1.42584

methodology.method_family: critical conceptual analysis with references to meta-analyses and respondent-based findings
methodology.study_design: critical analysis of AI ethics governance literature and guidelines; partial respondent-based discussion reported
methodology.sector: cross-sector public and private AI deployment examples in Brazil
methodology.technology_context: autonomous intelligent systems, machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, and chatbots/NLP cited as examples of AI use

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article critically addresses AI governance through ethical guidelines, regulation, and bioethics across public and private contexts, aligning with governance and regulated-domain dimensions. However, it does not center conversational systems, LLMs, or operational conversational governance mechanisms; chatbots appear only as a peripheral deployment example.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Extracted metadata misclassified publication type and title; only partial full text provided; respondent/survey methods referenced on page 8 but not fully described in excerpts.

appraisal.notes: Clear normative objective and governance focus, but limited transparency in the excerpts about any empirical respondent sample and its analysis.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is coherent for broad AI ethics governance, but methodological details of any survey component are unclear in the provided text, and direct relevance to conversational LLM governance in regulated settings is limited.

coding.subtheme: Limits of principled ethical guidelines and need for legal regulation

synthesis.main_claim: Governance of AI based on principled ethical guidelines is not sufficient to norm the AI industry and its developers; stronger professional training and legal regulation informed by bioethics are needed.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a critical philosophical analysis of AI ethics as a governance tool and proposes translating ethical contributions into legal terms via bioethics.
synthesis.limitations: Little is known about the effectiveness of ethics-as-governance; the provided excerpts do not substantively address conversational AI, LLMs, or operational governance controls.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence on ethics-based AI governance, regulation, and bioethics; not as central evidence for conversational LLM governance mechanisms.
